definition: To say what you think will happen before it happens.
example: Dark clouds made me predict that it would rain by noon.

options.text: To tell what already happened last week
To forget what you meant to say
To ask where something is kept
To say what will happen before it does

explanation: To predict is to say what you think will happen next. Nice work!

definition: A person who lives near you, such as in the next house.
example: Our neighbor waters our plants when we go away.

options.text: A person who lives close to your home
A person who teaches in your classroom
A person who sells food at a market
A person who drives a bus around town

explanation: A neighbor is someone who lives near you. Great job!

definition: A group of people who live, work or play in the same area.
example: Our community built a new playground in the park.

options.text: A single large building made of brick
A set of rules for a board game
A road that goes around a big city
A group of people who share an area

explanation: A community is a group of people who share an area. You got it!

definition: Something a family or group has done the same way for many years.
example: Baking pies together every fall is our family tradition.

options.text: A sudden change that nobody expected
A completely new idea no one has tried
A habit that only one person has
A custom passed down over many years

explanation: A tradition is a custom that is passed down over time. Well done!

definition: To look at two things to see how they are alike and different.
example: Let's compare the two maps to see which route is shorter.

options.text: To join two things into one whole
To check how two things are alike and different
To count how many things there are
To pick one thing and ignore the other

explanation: To compare is to see how two things are alike and different. Nice work!

definition: Something made by blending two or more things together.
example: The soup was a mixture of beans, corn and carrots.

options.text: Something made by blending different things
A thing that stays in one single solid piece
A part that breaks off from the whole
A place where many things are stored

explanation: A mixture is made by blending different things together. Great job!

definition: Something that flows and takes the shape of its container, like water or juice.
example: Pour the liquid slowly into the measuring cup.

options.text: Something hard that always keeps its own shape
Something that flows like water or juice
Something light that floats in the air
Something soft that you can squeeze

explanation: A liquid flows, like water or juice. You got it!

definition: A hard thing that keeps its own shape and does not flow.
example: Ice is a solid, but it turns to water when it melts.

options.text: Something that spills out and spreads flat
Something that floats up into the air
Something that is too tiny to be seen
Something that holds its own shape

explanation: A solid keeps its own shape instead of flowing. Well done!

definition: To turn around a center point, the way a wheel spins.
example: The fan blades rotate faster when you turn the dial up.

options.text: To move straight toward a target
To drop down from a high place
To turn around a center point
To slide back and forth on a line

explanation: To rotate is to turn around a center point. Nice work!

definition: To shake back and forth very quickly.
example: The guitar string will vibrate when you pluck it.

options.text: To stay perfectly still and silent
To shake back and forth very fast
To roll slowly across the floor
To float gently up into the air

explanation: To vibrate is to shake back and forth very fast. Great job!

definition: To soak up a liquid, light or heat.
example: A sponge can absorb a lot of spilled water.

options.text: To push something away from itself
To soak something up into itself
To pour something out of itself
To cut something into small pieces

explanation: To absorb is to soak something up. You got it!

definition: A steady position in which your weight is spread evenly so you do not fall.
example: She held her arms out to keep her balance on the narrow log.

options.text: A strong force that sends things flying away
A sudden stop caused by a heavy bump
A quick jump that carries you far
A steady position with weight spread out

explanation: Balance is a steady position that keeps you from falling. Well done!

definition: A large bowl-shaped hole in the ground or on the surface of a moon.
example: Through the telescope we saw a huge crater on the moon.

options.text: A tall hill with a pointed top
A deep ditch full of fast running water
A large bowl-shaped hole in the ground
A flat plain covered in tall grass

explanation: A crater is a large bowl-shaped hole. Nice work!

definition: The steady movement of water or air in one direction.
example: The swimmers let the river's current carry them downstream.

options.text: A tall wave that crashes down hard on the shore
A calm pool of still, quiet water
The steady movement of water in one direction
A deep hole at the bottom of a lake

explanation: A current is water or air moving steadily one way. Great job!

definition: A period of ten years.
example: My grandmother has lived in the same house for over a decade.

options.text: A period of ten whole weeks
A period of ten years
A period of ten full months
A period of a hundred years

explanation: A decade is a period of ten years. You got it!

definition: The amount of space between two places or things.
example: The distance from our house to school is about one mile.

options.text: The time it takes to finish a long chore
The weight of a heavy backpack
The amount of space between two places
The speed of a car on the road

explanation: Distance is the amount of space between two places. Well done!

definition: Facts or signs that show something is true.
example: Muddy paw prints were evidence that the dog had been in the garden.

options.text: Rules that tell you what to do next
A guess that nobody has checked yet
A made-up story told just for fun
Signs that show something is true

explanation: Evidence is a sign that shows something is true. Nice work!

definition: The hardened remains or print of a plant or animal from long ago, found in rock.
example: We found a fossil of a fern leaf inside a flat gray rock.

options.text: A print of a plant or animal in old rock
A shell that washed up on the beach last week
A seed that grows into a tall tree
A gem that is cut and polished by hand

explanation: A fossil is the print of a plant or animal in old rock. Great job!

definition: A huge, slow-moving mass of ice that covers land.
example: A glacier moves so slowly that you cannot see it change in a day.

options.text: A thick cloud of white fog above a quiet lake
A large pond of warm, still water
A huge, slow-moving river of ice on land
A fast stream of cold, rushing water

explanation: A glacier is a huge, slow-moving mass of ice. You got it!

definition: To look at something closely and carefully to check it.
example: Before the trip, we always inspect the bike tires.

options.text: To throw something away without looking
To paint something a bright color
To carry something up a long flight of stairs
To look at something closely and carefully

explanation: To inspect is to look closely and carefully. Well done!

definition: A thick forest in a warm, rainy place where many plants and animals live.
example: Vines hung from the tall trees of the jungle.

options.text: A thick, warm forest full of plants
A flat, dry land with few plants
A cold, icy field covered in snow
A sandy shore beside the sea

explanation: A jungle is a thick, warm forest full of plants and animals. Nice work!

definition: A light you can carry, set inside a case that protects it.
example: We hung a lantern from a branch so we could see at the campsite.

options.text: A tool for digging holes in soil
A cloth bag for carrying lunch
A frame for holding up a tent
A carried light inside a protective case

explanation: A lantern is a light you can carry in a case. Great job!

definition: A tool with moving parts that helps people do work.
example: This machine sorts the mail much faster than a person can.

options.text: A person who fixes cars and trucks
A tool with parts that move to do work
A room where people rest after work
A material used to build strong walls

explanation: A machine has moving parts that help people do work. You got it!

definition: To tell a story or explain what is happening.
example: I will narrate the story while you act it out.

options.text: To tell a story or say what is happening
To write down a list of numbers
To sing a song without any words
To listen quietly to a long, exciting story

explanation: To narrate is to tell a story or say what is happening. Well done!

definition: Something in food that helps a body or plant grow and stay healthy.
example: Calcium is a nutrient that helps keep your bones strong.

options.text: A dish served at the end of a meal
A spice that gives food a hot taste
A part of food that helps you grow
A way of cooking food over a fire

explanation: A nutrient is a part of food that helps you grow. Nice work!

definition: What you think or feel about something, which others may not share.
example: My opinion is that the blue kite looks better than the red one.

options.text: A fact that can be checked and then proved
What you think or feel about something
A rule that everyone has to follow
A question that has only one answer

explanation: An opinion is what you think or feel about something. Great job!

definition: A small wave on the surface of water.
example: A pebble made a ripple that spread across the pond.

options.text: A heavy stone at the bottom of a lake
A tiny wave on the top of water
A thin layer of ice on a pond
A tall pole that holds up a dock

explanation: A ripple is a tiny wave on the top of water. You got it!

definition: A set of questions asked to many people to learn what they think.
example: Our class made a survey to find out everyone's favorite lunch.

options.text: A set of questions asked to many people
A long trip taken across a country
A list of the answers on a test
A short test of your spelling words

explanation: A survey is a set of questions asked to many people. Well done!

definition: How hot or cold something is.
example: The temperature dropped overnight, so we wore warm coats.

options.text: How heavy or light something is
How loud or quiet something is
How warm or cool something is
How tall or short something is

explanation: Temperature tells how warm or cool something is. Nice work!

definition: A machine, such as a car or a bus, that carries people or things from place to place.
example: Every vehicle stopped when the light turned red.

options.text: A path that cars and trucks drive on
A machine that carries people or goods
A tool for fixing a flat tire
A lot where cars are parked overnight

explanation: A vehicle is a machine that carries people or goods. Great job!

definition: To make cloth or a basket by crossing strips over and under each other.
example: She likes to weave baskets out of long, dry grass.

options.text: To cut a piece of cloth into small squares
To glue sheets of paper onto a flat board
To cross strips over and under each other
To stretch a rope tight between two poles

explanation: To weave is to cross strips over and under each other. You got it!

definition: How much there is of something.
example: Add a small amount of salt to the soup.

options.text: How fast something is going
How old something has become
How much there is of something
How bright something looks

explanation: An amount tells how much there is of something. Well done!

definition: Something that blocks the way or keeps things apart.
example: A tall fence formed a barrier between the yard and the road.

options.text: Something that shows the way forward
Something that pulls things closer
Something that helps things move along
Something that blocks the way

explanation: A barrier is something that blocks the way. Nice work!

definition: A very heavy snowstorm with strong wind.
example: School was closed because of the blizzard.

options.text: A warm rain that falls in summer
A heavy snowstorm with strong wind
A bright arc of color after rain
A dry wind that blows over sand

explanation: A blizzard is a heavy snowstorm with strong wind. Great job!

definition: A period of one hundred years.
example: Our town's library was built more than a century ago.

options.text: A period of one hundred years
A period of ten whole years
A period of one thousand years
A period of one hundred days

explanation: A century is a period of one hundred years. You got it!

definition: The usual weather in a place over many years.
example: The climate in the desert is hot and dry all year.

options.text: The usual weather of a place over many years
The weather outside on one single sunny afternoon
The map that shows where a place is
The kind of soil that plants grow in

explanation: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years. Well done!

definition: A small group of things close together.
example: A cluster of grapes hung from the vine.

options.text: A single thing standing all alone
A small group of things close together
A long line of things in order
A pair of things that match exactly

explanation: A cluster is a small group of things close together. Nice work!

definition: To use something carefully so that it is not wasted.
example: We turn off the lights to conserve electricity.

options.text: To buy as much of something as you can
To use something without wasting it
To hide something where no one looks
To mix something with other things

explanation: To conserve is to use something without wasting it. Great job!

definition: A clear difference between two things when you look at them together.
example: There is a strong contrast between the dark sky and the bright moon.

options.text: A clear difference between two things
A perfect match between two things
A close link between two things
A mix made by joining two things

explanation: A contrast is a clear difference between two things. You got it!

definition: To say something clearly and with confidence so everyone can hear.
example: The coach will declare the winner at the end of the race.

options.text: To keep something secret from everyone
To whisper something only to yourself
To forget something said earlier
To say something clearly for all to hear

explanation: To declare is to say something clearly for all to hear. Well done!

definition: Easily broken or damaged, so it needs gentle handling.
example: The glass bird is delicate, so hold it with both hands.

options.text: Strong enough to last for years
Heavy and tough to lift or carry
Easy to break and needing care
Rough and bumpy on the surface

explanation: Delicate means easy to break and needing care. Nice work!

definition: One small piece of information about something.
example: One small detail in the photo, a tiny red door, caught my eye.

options.text: A small piece of information about something
The main idea of a whole story
The title printed on a book cover
The last line of a long poem

explanation: A detail is a small piece of information. Great job!

definition: To come out from a hidden or closed-in place.
example: The turtle began to emerge from its shell.

options.text: To step back into a hiding place
To come out into the open
To fall asleep in a quiet spot
To get stuck in a narrow gap

explanation: To emerge is to come out into the open. You got it!

definition: Whole, with nothing left out.
example: I read the entire book in one weekend.

options.text: Empty, with nothing inside it
Broken, with several pieces gone
Small, with only one part showing
Whole, with no part left out

explanation: Entire means whole, with no part left out. Well done!

definition: A building where workers and machines make things.
example: The toy factory makes thousands of puzzles each week.

options.text: A place where people go to read
A shop that sells fresh vegetables
A field where crops are grown
A building where things are made

explanation: A factory is a building where things are made. Nice work!

definition: Happening often or again and again.
example: We have frequent storms in spring, so I keep my umbrella by the door.

options.text: Happening just one time
Happening only on weekends
Happening often, again and again
Happening only once in a while

explanation: Frequent means happening often. Great job!

definition: A sheltered area of water by the shore where boats can stay safely.
example: The fishing boats returned to the harbor before sunset.

options.text: A safe place by the shore for boats
A wooden bridge over a wide river
A beach where children build sand castles
A narrow path beside a fast river

explanation: A harbor is a safe place by the shore for boats. You got it!

definition: To cover something so that heat stays in or out.
example: Workers will insulate the attic so the house stays warmer in winter.

options.text: To clean something with soap and warm water
To paint something a bright color
To lift something off the ground
To cover something to hold heat in or out

explanation: To insulate is to cover something to hold heat in or out. Well done!

definition: What something is made from, such as wood, metal or cloth.
example: Wood is a strong material for building a treehouse.

options.text: What an object is made from
The place where an object is kept
The reason an object was bought
The color an object is painted

explanation: Material is what an object is made from. Nice work!

definition: To turn old things, like paper or cans, into new things.
example: We recycle our bottles instead of throwing them away.

options.text: To toss old things in the trash
To bury old things deep in the ground
To turn old things into new things
To count old things one by one

explanation: To recycle is to turn old things into new things. Great job!
